name: Related Website Sets (retired)
plain: A declared group of sites that could share cookies. Removal postponed to Chrome 152 to 153.
meaning: Let one organisation list a primary plus associated and service sites (up to 5 associated, 3 service) that were treated as same party for storage access prompts. Retired Oct 2025 with requestStorageAccessFor; Related Website Partition discontinued.

access.revocation: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

limits.headline: Can't let a group of related sites share cookies in Chrome anymore
limits.user_action: Nothing. It would have happened when you moved between sites in the same group
can: Have let sites in one declared group share cookies
Have allowed embeds to use cookies without a prompt for sites in the group
cannot: Run in Chrome 152 or later, where removal was postponed
Work in Edge, Firefox or Safari
Add sites that were not declared

story.what_it_is: A list of sites owned by one group that were to share cookies. Retired.

marketing.name: Related Website Sets
marketing.pitch: Chrome pitched it as a way for sites of one organization to share cookies in limited, declared groups.

story.for_you: You never saw it. A company could list its own sites as one group. The browser would then let them share cookies without a prompt. It was retired in 2025.
story.for_makers: Big brands with many domains wanted to keep login across them. The list was a small fix to cookie blocking. It also let a company decide who counted as the same owner, which worried privacy groups.

use_cases.example: A news company with several sites kept one login across them.
A retailer shared a cart across its brand sites.
A game company shared login across its store, forums and game sites.
A social network used the group for one sign in across its apps.
An ad network could have shown the same ad profile across sites of one brand.
A software firm shared session cookies among its app and help domains.

technical_bounds: Primary site plus max 5 associated sites

abuse: Cross-site cookie sharing between a company's domains
